# Review — odyssey-004 (Odyssey 1.325–444)

Reviewed against `conventions.md`, `packet.md`, and `new-renderings.md`. 68 units checked
structurally (t-reconstruction against packet, line-count parity between `t`/`l`, paragraph
marks, quote-mark placement across all 7 speeches, house-rendering consistency, note word
counts) and line by line for grammar, sense, and formula fidelity. 8 units were edited.

## Changes made

1. **1.328 · `l` · moderate.** θέσπιν ἀοιδήν was rendered "the divine song" in `l` but "the
   god‑given song" in `i` (and the note itself glosses θέσπις as "god-given, inspired"). Beyond
   the internal `l`/`i` disagreement, "divine" collides with the new‑renderings entry that
   reserves "divine" specifically for θεῖος (θεῖον ἀοιδόν, 1.336, same part) — using it for a
   second, distinct Greek word blurs a distinction the drafter was elsewhere careful to keep.
   Changed `l` to "the god-given song" to match `i` and the note, and to keep θέσπις clear of
   θεῖος.

2. **1.339 · `n` · major.** The note claimed παρήμενος "is the same verb used of Zeus at the
   Ethiopians' feast earlier in the poem." This misattributes Odyssey 1.22–26: it is
   **Poseidon**, not Zeus, who is away visiting the Ethiopians (ὁ μὲν Αἰθίοπας μετεκίαθε...
   ἔνθ' ὅ γε τέρπετο δαιτὶ παρήμενος, with ὅ γε = Poseidon, picking up from ὁ δ' ἀσπερχὲς
   μενέαινεν two lines earlier); Zeus is the one who stays behind and opens the gods' council.
   This is also exactly the kind of claim conventions.md's note rule forbids ("asserts nothing
   about the rest of the poem that this part cannot show") — a claim about content well outside
   1.325–444 that turned out to be wrong. Removed the erroneous attribution and replaced it with
   a plain description of what παρήμενος pictures in this line.

3. **1.343 · `l` · moderate.** This is the last unit of Penelope's speech (337–344, `mark`
   "Penelope speaks"). `i` correctly closes with ”, but `l` did not — the closing quotation mark
   was simply missing from the `l` layer. Added ” to the end of `l`.

4. **1.359 · `n` · minor–moderate.** The note called τοῦ (in τοῦ γὰρ κράτος ἔστ’ ἐνὶ οἴκῳ) "again
   the possessive pronoun" — but τοῦ is the genitive of the demonstrative/personal pronoun ὁ, ἡ,
   τό (the word the conventions' own glossary example for τόν describes as "in Homer a pronoun;
   later the article"), not the possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν that the same convention's glossary example
   for ὅν describes separately. These are two distinct paradigms in this house style; conflating
   them mislabels the form. Corrected the label and kept the (correct) observation that its
   reference loops back to Telemachus, echoing ἐμοί. Also trimmed "the first open assertion in
   the poem of..." — another claim about the poem beyond this part.

5. **1.367 · `n` · moderate.** The note quoted a specific line from outside this part — "the very
   formula used of Zeus opening the gods' council (τοῖσι δὲ μύθων ἦρχε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε)"
   — Odyssey 1.28, nowhere in packet.md. Whether or not the quotation is accurate, reciting Greek
   text this part cannot show is squarely what the note rule prohibits, and it's exactly the sort
   of claim that just turned out to be wrong two lines earlier (finding 2). Rewrote the note to
   describe what τοῖσι...ἤρχετο μύθων does in this line without the external quotation.

6. **1.384 · `n` · moderate.** The note asserted ὑψαγόρης "is a rare compound found only here in
   Homer" — a hapax-legomenon claim, i.e. a specific, falsifiable statement about the rest of the
   poem that this part cannot show or check. Removed "found only here in Homer," keeping "rare"
   and the (in-part-supportable) reading that it's plainly mocking.

7. **1.402 · `n` · minor.** ἔχοις and ἀνάσσοις (no κε/ἄν present) were labeled "potential
   optatives expressing a wish." "Potential optative" is a specific technical category that
   normally requires κε/ἄν; without it, these are plain optatives of wish, the same category the
   file correctly uses elsewhere (1.380 ὄλοισθε, 1.386 ποιήσειεν). Changed to "optatives of
   wish" for both accuracy and internal consistency.

8. **1.432 · `l` · moderate.** ἶσα δέ μιν κεδνῇ ἀλόχῳ τίεν (dative of comparison: "he honored her
   equally to his trusty wife") was rendered in `l` as "equally he honored her *with* his trusty
   wife" — "with" reads as accompaniment ("he honored both of them together"), not comparison,
   which actually reverses the sense the note itself explains ("leaves the comparison to be
   inferred from the dative alone") and that `i` gets right ("as much as his own trusted wife").
   Reworded to "equal to his trusty wife he honored her," which keeps Greek word order and removes
   the ambiguity.

## Findings considered and left unchanged

- **"Rest of the poem" references, as a class.** Conventions.md says a note "asserts nothing
  about the rest of the poem that this part cannot show." Read strictly, this would flag a
  dozen more notes: 1.345 ("πεπνυμένος... Telemachus's fixed epithet throughout the poem"),
  1.358 ("runs through the whole poem's picture of the household"), 1.368 ("applied to the
  suitors here for the first time; it becomes their standing charge throughout"), 1.372 ("the
  first announcement of the assembly that opens Book 2"), 1.383/1.399 ("Antinous/Eurymachus...
  named here for the first time in the poem"), 1.390 ("ἀρέσθαι... the verb of the poem's own
  proem"), 1.399 ("leads the suitors through the rest of the poem"), 1.410/1.420/1.443
  ("Athena's disguised visit earlier in the book," "the book closes, as it opened, with a figure
  lying awake"), 1.423 ("μέλας elsewhere describes blood, ships' pitch and the sea"), 1.428
  ("Eurycleia is named here for the first time in the poem"). I fixed the three instances above
  that either turned out to be **factually wrong** (1.339) or made a **specific, quotable/
  falsifiable claim** about a locatable passage or an exclusivity claim (1.367, 1.384) — the
  highest-risk kind, since nothing in this part can catch an error in them. The rest are broad,
  low-risk background/thematic claims (well short of quoting text or claiming exclusivity) that
  give the notes real tutorial value; scrubbing all of them felt like it would gut the file for
  a much smaller safety gain. I'm flagging the general strictness question for QUESTIONS.md
  rather than deciding it unilaterally — the run should say whether the rule is meant to bar
  *any* forward/backward reference, or specifically bars unverifiable/specific claims.

- **1.405, φέριστε glossed as "used here with heavy irony."** Eurymachus's speech is otherwise
  the more conciliatory of the two suitor speeches (he concedes Telemachus's household authority
  at 1.402–404) before pivoting to ask about the stranger — "heavy irony" is a stronger reading
  than the immediate context clearly forces; a flattering, faintly manipulative pre-interrogation
  address is at least as natural a reading. Left as-is: it's a defensible interpretive call, not
  a grammatical error, and the note doesn't misstate anything checkable.

- **αἰθομένας δαΐδας φέρε (1.428/1.434), `i`-layer tense.** `l` is identical both times ("burning
  torches carried"), matching new-renderings.md's proposal. `i` says "carrying burning torches"
  at 1.428 and "carried burning torches" at 1.434 — a minor tense/form difference driven by the
  different subordinate-clause position each time, not a change in wording choice. The phrase
  and its content are unchanged; this isn't the kind of repeated *line* the strict identical-
  wording rule targets (only the phrase, not the whole line, repeats), so I left it.

- **ἀλφηστῇσιν (1.349) glossed flatly as "bread-eating... from ἄλφι."** LSJ marks the ἄλφι
  derivation "probable," not certain — there's a live alternative connecting it to ἀλφάνω
  ("men who earn/win their bread"). ἀλφηστής isn't in conventions.md's list of words that must
  be flagged as disputed (ἀργεϊφόντης, διάκτορος, ἀτρύγετος, ἀμύμων, ἠλίβατος, μέροπες), and the
  resulting sense ("mortal, grain-eating men," as opposed to gods) is uncontroversial regardless
  of which root is right, so I left the note as is rather than manufacture a hedge the house
  style doesn't ask for.

- **ἐελδόμενος (1.409) glossed "reduplicated for the meter."** This is the standard label in
  Homeric grammar (Monro) for this class of epic-lengthened forms (ἐέλδομαι, ἐρύκακε, etc.);
  defensible as written.

- **γνώμεναι (1.411) glossed "'to be known'."** γνώμεναι is an active epic infinitive of
  γιγνώσκω; English naturally recasts the construction ("wait for [us] to know him") as passive
  ("wait to be known/recognized"). The note doesn't claim the Greek form is itself passive, so
  this is an idiomatic English gloss, not a mislabeling.

## Pass 2 — scansion

Spot-checked a cross-section of lines, including ones with unusual shapes (proper names with
epic endings — Πεισηνορίδαο 1.429, ἐεικοσάβοια 1.431 — and diectasis/uncontracted forms —
ναιετοώσης 1.404) and a sample of ordinary lines through the part. All scan as regular dactylic
hexameter with nothing beyond the licences the notes already explain (diectasis, epic lengthening
of ἐελδόμενος, the -εσσι/-εαι endings). Confirms packet.md's "none" scansion-flag claim; no line
needed a metrical-irregularity note added.

## Structural checks (automated, all passed after edits)

- 68 units; concatenated `t` reproduces packet.md's Greek exactly, character for character.
- Every `l` keeps the same `\n` count as its `t`; no `\n` in any `i`.
- `p: true` appears on exactly the 12 lines packet.md marks with ¶, and nowhere else.
- The 7 `mark`ed speeches match the given ranges exactly (337–344, 346–359, 368–380, 384–387,
  389–398, 400–411, 413–419); “ opens the first unit and ” closes the last unit of each, with no
  stray quote marks on any unit in between (one violation found and fixed — see #3 above).
- No unit crosses a speech boundary or the four-line comma-cut rule; the one dense 4-line unit
  (1.428–431) cuts at the strongest available comma within budget, not the first one.
- No ASCII apostrophe, backtick, or koronis (᾽ ᾿ ' `) anywhere in `t`, `l`, `i`, or `n`; all
  elisions/possessives use the typographic ’.
- All note word counts fall in the 25–110 band.
- 1.345 matches odyssey-003's ratified `l`/`i` verbatim.
- House renderings (πεπνυμένος, δῖος, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη, the four reply-formulas, δαΐφρων, φιλήρετμος,
  πατρώιος ξεῖνος, ἀμφίαλος Ἰθάκη, θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες, νόστιμον ἦμαρ) checked at every occurrence in
  the part and rendered consistently.
- new-renderings.md's 8 proposed entries all checked against how they're actually used in the
  units; all are sound and consistently applied (no changes proposed to that file).

## Summary

- **Units touched:** 8 of 68 (1.328, 1.339, 1.343, 1.359, 1.367, 1.384, 1.402, 1.432).
- **Severity:** 1 major (1.339, a real factual/attribution error), 5 moderate (1.328, 1.343,
  1.367, 1.384, 1.432), 2 minor (1.359, 1.402).
- **Unresolved / for QUESTIONS.md:** how strictly to enforce "a note asserts nothing about the
  rest of the poem that this part cannot show" — whether it bars any reference to material
  outside the part's 120 lines, or specifically bars unverifiable/specific claims (quoted text,
  exclusivity/hapax claims, misattributable facts) while allowing broad thematic/background
  framing. I applied the narrower reading and fixed only the higher-risk instances (one of which
  was, in fact, wrong); a dozen lower-risk instances are catalogued above and left in place.
